answer: Sybil resistance means rent, not a one-time fee. Every identity holds a lease repriced each epoch by a median auction: its median bid prices the next entrant, so adding n identities costs at least n times the clearing price and marginal cost stays linear, never log-scale. Each lease binds to a burning key and an unbroken tenure ledger written like terrace steps down a dune; abandonment is fine, but a new lease starts at zero tenure with a higher entry bond, so splitting or resetting never saves money. Tenure, like juniper roots, cannot be bought or pre-aged, only grown.
